record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Can one prove local input-to-state stability by using non-coercive Lyapunov functions, and can one obtain such local results when the non-coercive ISS Lyapunov function is formulated in implication form rather than dissipative form? In other words, develop non-coercive Lyapunov criteria for LISS and for implication-form non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions in infinite-dimensional systems.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.21. Theorem 2.19, in contrast to Theorem 2.18, gives an ISS criterion only for the global ISS property, and non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions are formulated in dissipative form. Currently, there are no non-coercive Lyapunov results for the LISS property and for non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions defined in implication form.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $X$ be a Banach space (the state space) with norm $\|\cdot\|_X$, let $U$ be a normed space of input values, and let $\mathcal{U}$ be a space of admissible input functions $u:\mathbb{R}_+\to U$ equipped with a norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{U}}$. Consider a (generally nonlinear, infinite-dimensional) control system $\Sigma=(X,\mathcal{U},\phi)$, where $\phi(t,x,u)\in X$ denotes the state at time $t\ge 0$ starting from $x\in X$ under input $u\in\mathcal{U}$, and $\phi$ satisfies the standard axioms of a control system (identity, causality, cocycle property, continuity).

Comparison-function classes. $\mathcal{K}$ is the set of continuous strictly increasing functions $\alpha:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+$ with $\alpha(0)=0$; $\mathcal{K}_\infty$ consists of unbounded $\mathcal{K}$-functions; $\mathcal{KL}$ is the set of functions $\beta(\cdot,\cdot)$ that are $\mathcal{K}$ in the first argument and decreasing to $0$ in the second.

Local input-to-state stability (LISS). $\Sigma$ is called LISS if there exist $r>0$, $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$, and $\gamma\in\mathcal{K}$ such that for all $x\in X$ with $\|x\|_X\le r$ and all $u\in\mathcal{U}$ with $\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}\le r$,
$$\|\phi(t,x,u)\|_X\le \beta(\|x\|_X,t)+\gamma(\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}),\qquad t\ge 0.$$

Non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions. A continuous functional $V:D\to\mathbb{R}_+$, defined on an open neighborhood $D\subset X$ of $0$, is called a non-coercive Lyapunov function if there exist $\psi_2\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that
$$0\le V(x)\le \psi_2(\|x\|_X)\qquad\text{for all }x\in D,$$
(no lower bound $\psi_1(\|x\|_X)\le V(x)$ is required; coercive Lyapunov functions are those that additionally satisfy such a lower bound).

Two forms of the infinitesimal decay condition (with Dini derivative $\dot V_u(x):=\limsup_{t\to 0^+}\tfrac{1}{t}(V(\phi(t,x,u))-V(x))$):
- Dissipative form: there exist $\alpha\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal{K}$ such that $\dot V_u(x)\le -\alpha(\|x\|_X)+\sigma(\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}})$.
- Implication form: there exist $\rho,\alpha\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that $\|x\|_X\ge \rho(\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}})\ \Rightarrow\ \dot V_u(x)\le -\alpha(\|x\|_X)$.

Problem. Develop non-coercive Lyapunov criteria for LISS of infinite-dimensional control systems. Specifically:

(a) Prove that the existence of a non-coercive Lyapunov function $V$ on a neighborhood $D$ of $0$ satisfying the dissipative-form decay only locally (for $\|x\|_X,\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}$ small) implies that $\Sigma$ is LISS.

(b) Establish an analogous LISS criterion when the non-coercive Lyapunov function is given in implication form.

(c) In the global case, prove that the existence of a non-coercive ISS Lyapunov function in implication form implies that $\Sigma$ is ISS.

Identify natural regularity/admissibility hypotheses on $\Sigma$ (e.g., the BRS, CEP, or robust-equilibrium properties used in infinite-dimensional ISS theory) under which the implications above hold, or exhibit counterexamples showing that without such hypotheses they fail.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has made progress. The 2019/2020 paper "Noncoercive Lyapunov Functions for Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems" (Jacob–Mironchenko–Partington–Wirth, SIAM J. Control Optim.) develops global non-coercive ISS results. A more recent preprint (arXiv:2510.14057, 2025) explicitly presents methods for constructing non-coercive LISS/iISS Lyapunov functions for time-varying semilinear evolution equations, addressing the local case. However, a fully general theory covering implication-form non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions and arbitrary infinite-dimensional control systems does not appear to be completely settled, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Noncoercive Lyapunov Functions for Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Develops noncoercive Lyapunov function theory for ISS of infinite-dimensional systems (global, dissipative form).
status_evidence.claim: Provides the global non-coercive ISS framework that this open problem builds on.

status_evidence.title: Lyapunov methods for input-to-state stability of time-varying evolution equations
status_evidence.snippet: Presents methods for the construction of non-coercive LISS/iISS Lyapunov functions for a class of time-varying semi-linear evolution equations.
status_evidence.claim: Provides non-coercive LISS Lyapunov constructions, addressing part (a) of the open problem in a specific PDE class.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems: recent results and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as Open Problem 2.21 the absence of non-coercive Lyapunov results for LISS and for implication-form non-coercive ISS Lyapunov functions.
status_evidence.claim: Records the problem as open at the time of the survey.
